# Implementation Accelerator Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Prepared by:** AI Governance Academy
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, five consecutive working days, US$25,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, and has about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage. Its AI use spans three stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

**Regulatory drivers:** the EU AI Act and GDPR.

**Incumbent frameworks:**
* An ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system.
* An ISO 9001 quality management system.
* An internal audit function.

**Audit finding:** in June 2026, an internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

**Stated constraints:**
* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

**Stated objective:** "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits

**Timeline.** A decision is expected by 15 December 2026, and the stated objective sets Q2 2027 as the point by which governance should be in place. The Implementation Accelerator produces the foundation of an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) in one working week. That leaves the period before Q2 2027 for three things:
* adoption of the artifacts through Tamarack Instruments governance;
* works council consultation;
* controls specific to the visual inspection pilot.

The five-day format also concentrates the required roles into a single sustained build. That avoids a sequence of separate meetings spread across several months.

**Certification target.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year, and the start date is not yet fixed. Every artifact will be structured for future ISO/IEC 42001 conformity work. The aim is readiness. The program does not promise certification or audit results, and it makes no claim about any future SOC 2 (System and Organization Controls 2) outcome.

**Audit finding.** Day 2 produces an AI system inventory designed to respond to the June 2026 finding. Whether the inventory satisfies the finding is a determination for the internal audit function.

**Budget.** The Accelerator price of US$25,000 sits within the stated approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

**Principles.** The week is built on three principles, which shape decision rights, review gates and accountability in every artifact:
* **Slow AI:** deliberate adoption ahead of speed.
* **Informed Intent:** each AI use has a documented purpose and understood risks.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human.**

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The program sequences dependencies explicitly. The charter precedes the policies, and the inventory precedes the risk register.

The working method draws on three frameworks:
* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
* AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), as the reference for executive and board reporting.

| Day | Build focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Governance charter and roles | Decision rights across the legal, security, quality, data, plant management and internal audit roles named for the build team. Works council consultation is recorded as a required step before any AI use touches production staff. The executive checkpoint confirms scope and principles. |
| 2 | AI system inventory and classification | Seeded with the three known systems: chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting. Fields include lifecycle stage, operating jurisdiction, data residency and EU AI Act orientation category. Designed to respond to the June 2026 audit finding. |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessment plus risk register | Assessment method and register built on the Day 2 inventory. Risk statements are seeded as drafts for Tamarack Instruments validation. Visual inspection is given priority because of the Q2 2027 objective. |
| 4 | Core policies and operating procedures | Policies cover acceptable use, lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, and incident response and change management. They reflect the EU customer data constraint and the works council consultation requirement. |
| 5 | Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout | Evidence index structured for future ISO/IEC 42001 conformity work. A prioritized 90-day plan sequenced toward the Q2 2027 objective. Executive readout at the checkpoint. |

**Regulatory note.** EU AI Act and GDPR classification and mapping within the inventory and policies is orientation only. For example, this applies to how each of the three systems might be categorized under the EU AI Act. Confirm with external counsel. The United States is listed as an operating jurisdiction, and no United States regulatory driver has been identified. Whether any United States requirements apply is a question to confirm at intake.

**Attachment to incumbent frameworks.** Each artifact is designed to attach to the existing ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system, the ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function rather than stand alone. The specific attachment point within each is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake:
* **ISO/IEC 27001:** the risk methodology, policy hierarchy or document control artifact the AIMS should link to.
* **ISO 9001:** the inspection, nonconformity or change control artifact the AIMS should link to.
* **Internal audit:** how the function will receive the evidence index.

## 4. Artifacts Tamarack Instruments Owns at Close

All artifacts are delivered into the Tamarack Instruments document system and owned by Tamarack Instruments. Each leaves the week at draft or reviewed status, and adoption follows Tamarack Instruments governance.

1. AI Governance Charter (purpose, scope, roles, decision rights, meeting cadence)
2. Roles and Decision Rights Matrix
3. AI System Inventory and Classification Schema, with the three known systems as first entries
4. AI Risk and Impact Assessment Method
5. AI Risk Register, with seeded risk statements labeled as drafts for Tamarack Instruments validation
6. AI Acceptable Use Policy
7. AI Lifecycle Governance Policy
8. AI Vendor and Supplier Governance Policy
9. AI Incident Response and Change Management Procedure
10. Evidence Model and Evidence Index, mapping each artifact to the assurance question it answers
11. Prioritized 90-Day Implementation Plan with owners
12. Executive Readout Pack

## 5. Team Composition Requested

The build team is requested to attend the full week:

| Role | Contribution requested |
|---|---|
| General Counsel | Decision rights, regulatory orientation, policy review |
| CISO | Security and data residency requirements, incident response linkage |
| Head of Quality | Quality management linkage, change management, inspection-related controls |
| Head of Data | Inventory data, data governance fields, forecasting use case inputs |
| German plant manager | Production line context for visual inspection, works council requirements |
| Two internal auditors | Evidence model design and assurance questions |

**Executive checkpoint attendees.** Days 1 and 5 include executive checkpoints. The attendees are `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

**Internal audit independence.** Two internal auditors are named in the build team. Their mode of participation will be confirmed at intake, as builders, advisors or observers, so that the independence of the internal audit function is preserved for later review of the same artifacts.

## 6. Logistics and Price

**Format:** five consecutive working days of live virtual working sessions with structured build time.

**Dates:** to be confirmed at intake.

**Data handling:** the program does not require access to customer data. Artifacts are built directly in the Tamarack Instruments document system, and the system and its hosting location are `Unknown`, to be confirmed at intake. This keeps the work consistent with the constraint that customer data stays in the EU.

**Price:** US$25,000.

## 7. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. Proposed dates for the five-day week.
2. Names of executive checkpoint attendees for Days 1 and 5.
3. The participation mode of the two internal auditors.
4. Attachment points within the ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system, the ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function.
5. The document system that will hold the artifacts, and its hosting location.
6. Whether any part of the Accelerator itself requires prior works council consultation.
7. Whether any United States requirements should be included in regulatory orientation.
8. Ownership of each of the three known AI systems, to be recorded in the inventory.

## 8. Next Step

The proposed next step is a 45-minute intake session with Dana Whitfield to confirm the questions above and fix dates. On confirmation, the program will issue the Day 1 preparation pack and the build calendar.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
